strands.name: Strand A: Scientific Investigation Skills and Career Exploration

overalls.title: Scientific Investigation Skills
overalls.description: demonstrate scientific investigation skills (related to both inquiry and research) in the four areas of skills (initiating and planning, performing and recording, analysing and interpreting, and communicating)

specifics.description: I can ask scientific questions, make predictions, and plan safe investigations.
I can conduct experiments, collect accurate data, and organize it effectively.
I can analyse and interpret data, identify sources of error, and draw evidence-based conclusions.
I can communicate my findings using scientific language, appropriate formats, and precise measurements.

overalls.title: Career Exploration
overalls.description: identify and describe a variety of careers related to the fields of science under study, and identify scientists, including Canadians, who have made contributions to those fields

specifics.description: I can identify science-related careers and describe the education and training required.
I can describe the contributions of Canadian scientists to the fields under study.

strands.name: Strand B: Biology: Tissues, Organs, and Systems

overalls.title: Relating Science to Technology, Society, and the Environment
overalls.description: analyse some current technologies or substances that have an impact on human tissues, organs, or systems, and evaluate their effects on human health

specifics.description: I can evaluate how medical technologies, substances, and environmental factors affect human health.

overalls.title: Developing Skills of Investigation and Communication
overalls.description: investigate cell division, cell specialization, and the organization of systems in animals, including humans, using various laboratory techniques

specifics.description: I can use scientific terminology to investigate cells, mitosis, and cell specialization in the human body.
I can investigate health problems and the organization of organ systems using dissection or research.

overalls.title: Understanding Basic Concepts
overalls.description: demonstrate an understanding of the hierarchical organization of cells, from tissues, to organs, to systems in animals, including humans

specifics.description: I can explain the cell cycle and how specialized cells, tissues, and organs form body systems.
I can describe the functions of human body systems and how they interact for survival.

strands.name: Strand C: Chemistry: Chemical Reactions and Their Practical Applications

overalls.title: Relating Science to Technology, Society, and the Environment
overalls.description: analyse how chemical reactions are employed in common products and processes, and assess the safety and environmental hazards associated with them

specifics.description: I can analyse how chemical reactions are used in everyday products and workplace processes, including associated hazards.

overalls.title: Developing Skills of Investigation and Communication
overalls.description: investigate, through inquiry, the characteristics of simple chemical reactions

specifics.description: I can investigate simple chemical reactions and represent them using word equations, models, and balanced equations.
I can investigate acids, bases, neutralization reactions, and classify common substances using indicators.

overalls.title: Understanding Basic Concepts
overalls.description: demonstrate an understanding of simple chemical reactions and the language and ways to represent them

specifics.description: I can write names, formulae, and balanced chemical equations for simple compounds and reactions.
I can describe neutralization reactions and use the pH scale to classify acids and bases.

strands.name: Strand D: Earth and Space Science: Earth's Dynamic Climate

overalls.title: Relating Science to Technology, Society, and the Environment
overalls.description: analyse effects of human activity on climate change, and effects of climate change on living things and natural systems

specifics.description: I can analyse how human activities affect climate change and how climate change impacts living things and natural systems.

overalls.title: Developing Skills of Investigation and Communication
overalls.description: investigate various natural and human factors that have an impact on climate change and global warming

specifics.description: I can investigate factors that affect climate change using models, simulations, and research.
I can investigate my personal carbon footprint and compare different perspectives on climate change.

overalls.title: Understanding Basic Concepts
overalls.description: demonstrate an understanding of various natural and human factors that contribute to climate change and global warming

specifics.description: I can explain the natural and anthropogenic greenhouse effect and how heat is transferred in the climate system.
I can identify the causes, sources, and indicators of global climate change, including Canada's contributions.

strands.name: Strand E: Physics: Light and Applications of Optics

overalls.title: Relating Science to Technology, Society, and the Environment
overalls.description: analyse how properties of light and colour are applied in technology and the impact of these technologies on society

specifics.description: I can analyse how colour theory and optical technologies are applied in everyday devices and their impact on society.

overalls.title: Developing Skills of Investigation and Communication
overalls.description: investigate, through inquiry, properties of light, and predict its behaviour in mirrors and as it passes through different media

specifics.description: I can investigate reflection and refraction of light using experiments, ray diagrams, and mirrors.
I can investigate how light interacts with different materials and how colour is produced and perceived.

overalls.title: Understanding Basic Concepts
overalls.description: demonstrate an understanding of characteristics and properties of light, particularly with respect to reflection and refraction and the addition and subtraction of colour

specifics.description: I can explain the properties of light, including reflection, refraction, and the electromagnetic spectrum.
I can use additive and subtractive colour theory to explain how colour is produced and perceived in various technologies.
